content_preview.title: Meta Launches Muse Code, a Terminal AI Coding Agent Built to Take On Claude Code and Codex
content_preview.summary: Meta released the beta of Muse Code, a terminal-based AI coding agent powered by Muse Spark 1.2, undercutting Anthropic's pricing to compete with Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Meta released a beta version of Muse Code this week, a terminal-based AI coding agent that the company is positioning against Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/05/meta-launches-muse-code-an-ai-agent-for-large-code-bases/). The tool is Meta's first coding-specific product built on [Meta Superintelligence Labs](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/05/meta-takes-anthropic-openai-first-ai-coding-agent-muse-code/)' newest mod...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (618 words) with clear Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Analysis sections. Direct quotes are clearly attributed, technical claims (parallel sub-agent worktrees, event log/crash recovery, pricing tiers) are specific and traceable to sources.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 sources. source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch): confirms Zuckerberg quotes on 'complete software engineering tasks across large repos' and the 'fans out to separate sub-agents working in parallel in isolated worktrees' / 'no collisions' quote verbatim. source-1.html.gz (SiliconANGLE): confirms Alexandr Wang leads Superintelligence Labs, confirms 'Powered by Muse Spark 1.2' via the embedded Zuckerberg tweet, confirms the CNBC quote 'more than 10-times cheaper' and the pay-as-you-go/contributor-tier data-sharing tradeoff. source-3.html.gz (9to5Mac): confirms beta availability for macOS/Linux, the exact install command `curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | bash`, no dedicated GUI, the local event log/crash-recovery detail, and the Muse Spark timeline (original Muse Spark replaced Llama in April 2026, Muse Spark 1.1 in July 2026). Engadget (source-2) returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) at snapshot time with no archive.org fallback captured, so per Step 3b I fetched the live URL via WebFetch as a last resort: it returned the exact pricing figures cited in the article verbatim ('$1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens', contributor tier '$0.10 per million input tokens and $0.20 per million output tokens', and the Anthropic Sonnet 5 comparison '$3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens'). All four sources fully support their attributed claims; no misattribution or hallucinated quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (pricing figures, install command, quotes, org structure, product timeline) traces exactly to its cited source. The internal link to the April 2026 Muse Spark launch article resolves to an existing published article.
